newsitem.title: GERMANY: N.Europe rapeseed prices move up on tightness.
newsitem.headline: N.Europe rapeseed prices move up on tightness.

text.p: Rapeseed tightness in Northern Europe caused buyers' price rises this week although rape products eased in line with the Chicago soy complex, brokers said on Friday.
November buyers were at 468 marks free Hamburg, down from 470 marks on Thursday, but up three marks on the week.
"Sellers are reluctant to part with seed and crushers do need to make selective purchases to keep busy," one broker said, also citing Scandinavian and Polish buying interest.
Rapeseed buyers at German delivery points other than Hamburg pegged November at 445-465 marks compared with 437.50-457.50 marks offered for October last week.
But the November position on the Paris Matif futures exchange was last at 449 marks, down two from last night and compared with a 456-459 marks bid/offer range last Friday.
Rape oil prices took some support from the prospect of possible disruption from consumer opposition to genetically modified U.S. soybeans, which made consumers favour rapeseed.

Germany's subsidiary of Anglo-Dutch group Unilever, under pressure from environmentalist and consumer groups, said on Thursday it would stop using soy oil derived from the new beans in its products in Germany.
But the premium of Nov-Jan rape oil cif Rotterdam eased to 2.50 guilders per 100 kg fob mill at 91.50 guilders versus four guilders earlier this week in sluggish dealings.
"Rape oil followed soy oil lower and the Unilever case might be isolated and have little impact," one trader said.
"But if other wholesalers joined in the soy oil boycott, this could become good news for rape oil sellers, because there are few other alternatives to U.S. soy oil."
"Equally important could be a strict labelling regulation in the EU, which could identify gene-altered soya and through that fact alone might create a negative image," he added.
Local rape meal sellers (34 percent protein) were 0.25-0.75 mark down from last week at 30.00-30.50 marks/100 kg (Oct/Nov), with Dec/Jan meal steady at 29.75 marks.
Nov/Jan rape oil was at 81.00 marks/100 kg, down 2.75 on the week and Feb/April oil was at 84.50 marks, down 1.50.
